title: Advance decomposition only through per-candidate keep/pivot/kill verdicts

facts.note: Needs an observer for an active planner decomposition session (proposing heuristics, analogs, main jobs, wagons, features, WMBTs, trains, interlockings, contracts, acceptances).
Needs an observer that links each authored artifact (atdd author writer call) to the operator verdict on its candidate.
Whether operator prose amounts to keep, pivot or kill is judged (normalised by the natural-language-normalization convention).

fires: The planner proposes a wagon, feature, WMBT or acceptance candidate and is about to write its artifact.
The operator pivots a candidate with a named modification and the planner considers writing it without re-confirmation.
The operator kills every candidate at a granularity.
The operator keeps a heuristic, analog or main job candidate.
doesNotFire: Editing an already-kept artifact outside a decomposition session (e.g. fixing a typo in an existing acceptance).
Coder work implementing an already-planned acceptance.
Reading or reviewing plans without proposing new candidates.

given: A decomposition session where the planner proposes candidates (heuristic, analog, main job, wagon, feature, WMBT, acceptance, etc.).
when: The planner would advance past a candidate or act on it.
then: Advance each candidate only on the operator's individual keep, pivot or kill verdict for that candidate.
prefer: Pivot: apply the operator's named modification, then re-confirm.
Kill: reject; if all candidates at a granularity are killed, re-propose.
Write an artifact only after a keep at a final granularity (wagon, feature, WMBT, train, interlocking, contract, acceptance).
Heuristic, analog, main job are reasoning granularities: real candidates, but a keep records the decision and writes no artifact.
avoid: Advancing a candidate that has no individual verdict (several individually assigned verdicts may be delivered together).
Writing an artifact before a final-granularity keep, or a pivot before re-confirmation.
Erroring on a kept reasoning-level candidate, or recording kill when the operator kept it.
why: Per-unit verdicts keep the operator in control and recorded decisions truthful; only final granularities map to an author writer.
evidence: Each authored artifact traces to a recorded keep verdict (or a re-confirmed pivot) on that candidate at a final granularity.
Kept heuristics/analogs/main jobs appear as recorded decisions with no artifact and no dispatch error.
All-killed granularities are followed by a re-proposal, not by an artifact.
Every advanced candidate has its own recorded verdict.
verifier_detail: Final granularities (resolve to an atdd author writer): wagon, feature, WMBT, train, interlocking, contract, acceptance.

Reasoning granularities (decision recorded, no artifact): heuristic, analog, main job. Author dispatch must not raise on a kept reasoning-granularity candidate (regression of #1929); kill must not be the only verdict that keeps a session authorable.
audit: final_granularity made explicit by #1929: the author dispatch used to RAISE on a kept heuristic, which left kill — the verdict that records the opposite of what happened — as the only one that kept a session authorable.
